--- title: "Tariff exposure by HTS chapter" subtitle: "Where duty concentrates in an import book, and what moves it" date: last-modified author: "Jacob Gray" categories: [SQL, Python, Tariffs] draft: true --- ::: {.finding-box} [The headline number. Something in the shape of: duty exposure concentrates in [N] HTS chapters accounting for [X]% of value but [Y]% of duty paid, and the gap between those two figures is where the money is.] ::: ## The question Duty is not spread evenly across an import book. A small number of tariff lines usually carry most of the cost, and those lines are where reclassification review, first sale valuation, or a sourcing change pays for itself. The question is where to look first, and how much a plausible change is worth before anyone spends time on it. ## The data ::: {.provenance}
Source
USITC DataWeb for import value and calculated duty by HTS; the HTSUS for current rates.
Coverage
[Years], U.S. imports for consumption, [chapters].
Retrieved
[Date]
Known limits
Aggregate national data, not any one importer's entries. Section 301 and IEEPA rates change; this reflects the schedule as of [date]. Rates of duty also depend on country of origin and trade program eligibility, which aggregate data flattens.
::: ## Approach [Sketch, to replace with what you actually did:] - Load HTS-level import value and duty into SQLite, keyed on the 10-digit code. - Join the applicable general rate, plus any Section 301 or IEEPA additional rate, on the chapter or subheading. - Compute effective duty rate per line, and rank by absolute duty paid rather than by rate — a 2% rate on a large line beats a 25% rate on a small one. - Model one or two concrete scenarios: shifting origin for the top lines, or reclassifying where the code looks contestable. ```{sql} #| eval: false select substr(hts_code, 1, 4) as heading, sum(customs_value) as value, sum(calculated_duty) as duty, sum(calculated_duty) * 1.0 / nullif(sum(customs_value), 0) as effective_rate from imports where year = 2025 group by heading order by duty desc limit 20; ``` ## What I found [Result and one chart. Rank chapters by duty, and show effective rate against value so the outliers are visible.] ## What I would do differently [Name the weakness. Likely candidates: aggregate data hides origin mix, the scenarios assume a sourcing change is feasible when qualification and lead time often make it not, and duty is only part of landed cost.] --- *Code for this project: [GitHub](https://github.com/YOUR-GITHUB-USERNAME/REPO).*
